<style>
  :root{
    /* Canonical brand tokens — PlotNua Brand Package v1.0. Do not alter. */
    --brand-green:#1F3B2E; --brand-ivory:#F2EFE6; --brand-sage:#8FAF8A;
    --cream:#F2EFE6; --paper:#F8F5EC; --ink:#1F3B2E; --soft:#55605A;
    --accent:#4F6B4A; --oak:#8B6F4E;
  }
  *{box-sizing:border-box; margin:0; padding:0;}
  html{scroll-behavior:smooth;}
  body{ font-family:'Work Sans',sans-serif; background:var(--paper); color:var(--ink); overflow-x:hidden; }
  h1,h2,h3{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:-.01em; }
  h1,h2{ font-weight:700; }

  .reveal{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(6px); transition:opacity 1.1s ease, transform 1.1s ease; }
  .reveal.in{ opacity:1; transform:none; }

  /* ---- fixed brand mark (unchanged from Brand Integration v1) ---- */
  .brand-mark{
    position:fixed; top:22px; left:22px; z-index:50;
    display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center;
    width:46px; height:46px; padding:0;
    background:var(--brand-ivory);
    border-radius:12px;
    box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(31,59,46,.16), 0 0 0 1px rgba(31,59,46,.07);
    opacity:0; transition:opacity 1.6s ease, transform .4s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), box-shadow .4s ease;
    text-decoration:none;
  }
  .brand-mark:hover{ transform:scale(1.06); box-shadow:0 5px 16px rgba(31,59,46,.20), 0 0 0 1px rgba(31,59,46,.09); }

  /* RESULTS-003 PART D — THE FLOATING BACK.
     Identical to the control on Results and My Plot: same corner, same 44px
     minimum height, same radius, paper ground, hairline border and shadow,
     same type. Only the label and destination differ, because they must.

     It does not fight the brand mark. Measured: .brand-mark is fixed at
     TOP:22px left:22px, this is fixed at BOTTOM:22px left:22px. Opposite
     ends of the screen at every viewport. (I twice deferred this work on the
     stated grounds that they shared a corner. They never did.)

     z-index 60 sits above the page and below .am-modal-overlay (200), so an
     open modal covers it rather than having it float over a dialog. */
  .pn-return{
    position:fixed; left:22px; bottom:22px; z-index:60;
    display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px;
    min-height:44px; padding:11px 17px 11px 14px;
    background:var(--paper, #F8F5EC); color:var(--ink, #1F3B2E);
    border:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.16); border-radius:24px;
    box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(31,59,46,.13);
    font-family:'Work Sans',sans-serif; font-size:14px; font-weight:500;
    text-decoration:none; cursor:pointer;
    -webkit-appearance:none; appearance:none;
  }
  .pn-return:hover{ border-color:rgba(31,59,46,.3); }
  .pn-return-arrow{ font-size:15px; line-height:1; }
  @media (max-width:600px){
    .pn-return{ left:16px; bottom:16px; padding:10px 15px 10px 12px; font-size:13.5px; }
  }
  .brand-mark.in{ opacity:1; }
  .brand-mark img{ display:block; width:34px; height:34px; border-radius:8px; }
  @media(max-width:720px){
    .brand-mark{ top:16px; left:16px; width:40px; height:40px; }
    .brand-mark img{ width:30px; height:30px; }
  }

  /* ================= DISCOVERY — HERO =================
     Same visual grammar as the About page hero: a single still image,
     bottom-anchored copy, warm ivory serif type. This is the master
     template every future Discovery reuses, so the hero deliberately
     stays close to the About page's pattern rather than inventing a
     new one — consistency here is what makes the site feel like one
     continuous place, not a stitched-together set of templates. */
  .d-hero{ position:relative; width:100%; height:88vh; height:88svh; min-height:540px; overflow:hidden; background:var(--ink); }
  .d-hero img{
    width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:cover; display:block;
    transform:scale(1.03); opacity:0;
    transition:opacity 1.8s ease-out, transform 6s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1);
  }
  .d-hero img.on{ opacity:1; transform:scale(1); }
  .d-hero-scrim{ position:absolute; inset:0;
    background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(15,14,10,.14) 0%, rgba(15,14,10,0) 32%, rgba(15,14,10,.10) 60%, rgba(15,14,10,.60) 100%); }
  .d-hero-copy{ position:absolute; z-index:2; inset:auto 0 0 0; padding:0 8vw 10vh; text-align:center; }
  /* HERO EYEBROW — ADAPTIVE COLOUR (Master Standard).
     The eyebrow is an orientation label, not a brand element. On this hero
     --brand-sage (luminance 0.36) sat inside the luminance range of the
     plaster wall behind it (0.32-0.49) and washed out; no shadow can
     separate a colour from a background it matches in lightness.
     It therefore uses the same --brand-ivory as h1 / .subtitle / .intro,
     with the same shadow family as .intro. Font, size, weight, tracking
     and position are unchanged. */
  .d-hero-copy .eyebrow{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(10px); transition:opacity 1s ease, transform 1s ease;
    font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.18em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--brand-ivory); margin-bottom:20px;
    text-shadow:0 1px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.28); }
  .d-hero-copy h1{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(10px); transition:opacity 1s ease .1s, transform 1s ease .1s;
    color:var(--brand-ivory); font-size:clamp(32px,5vw,58px); line-height:1.14; text-shadow:0 2px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.32); }
  .d-hero-copy .subtitle{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(10px); transition:opacity 1s ease .18s, transform 1s ease .18s;
    margin:18px auto 0; max-width:32ch; font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-style:italic; font-weight:400;
    color:var(--brand-ivory); font-size:clamp(16px,1.9vw,21px); line-height:1.55; text-shadow:0 1px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.3); }
  .d-hero-copy .intro{ opacity:0; transform:translateY(10px); transition:opacity 1s ease .26s, transform 1s ease .26s;
    margin:24px auto 0; max-width:50ch; font-family:'Work Sans',sans-serif; font-weight:300;
    color:var(--brand-ivory); font-size:clamp(14px,1.4vw,16px); line-height:1.75; text-shadow:0 1px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.28); }
  .d-hero-copy.in .eyebrow, .d-hero-copy.in h1, .d-hero-copy.in .subtitle{ opacity:1; transform:none; }
  .d-hero-copy.in .intro{ opacity:.86; transform:none; }

  /* ================= ARTICLE RHYTHM (shared with About) ================= */
  .article{ max-width:1040px; margin:0 auto; padding:0 7vw; }
  .article-section{ padding:9.5vh 0; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.06); }
  .article-section:last-of-type{ border-bottom:none; }
  .article-section .kicker{ font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.16em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--accent); margin-bottom:19px; }
  .article-section h2{ font-size:clamp(26px,3.4vw,40px); line-height:1.32; max-width:19ch; margin-bottom:26px; }
  .article-section p{ color:var(--soft); font-size:17px; line-height:1.85; max-width:60ch; }
  .article-section p + p{ margin-top:20px; }

  /* ---- The Spark — the emotional opening line of every Discovery.
     Deliberately the quietest, largest moment on the page: one
     sentence, generous whitespace, nothing else competing with it. ---- */
  .spark{ position:relative; padding:12vh 7vw; text-align:center; background:var(--paper); overflow:hidden; }
  .spark::before{ content:''; position:absolute; top:0; left:0; right:0; height:16vh;
    background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(20,26,20,.05) 0%, rgba(20,26,20,0) 100%); pointer-events:none; }
  .spark p{ position:relative; font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-style:italic; font-weight:400; color:var(--ink);
    font-size:clamp(25px,3.6vw,40px); line-height:1.5; max-width:21ch; margin:0 auto; letter-spacing:-.005em; }

  /* ---- Imagine Your Property — a second full-width photograph with
     minimal text; this is a mood beat, not an information beat. ---- */
  .imagine-photo{ position:relative; width:100%; height:84vh; height:84svh; min-height:460px; overflow:hidden; background:var(--ink); }
  .imagine-photo img{ width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:cover; display:block; }
  .imagine-photo::before, .imagine-photo::after{ content:''; position:absolute; left:0; right:0; height:5vh; z-index:2; pointer-events:none; }
  .imagine-photo::before{ top:0; background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(248,245,236,.5) 0%, rgba(248,245,236,0) 100%); }
  .imagine-photo::after{ bottom:0; background:linear-gradient(0deg, rgba(242,239,230,.5) 0%, rgba(242,239,230,0) 100%); }
  .imagine-photo .caption{ position:absolute; z-index:3; left:0; right:0; bottom:0; padding:7vh 8vw;
    background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(15,14,10,0) 0%, rgba(15,14,10,.42) 100%); text-align:center; }
  .imagine-photo .caption p{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-style:italic; font-weight:400;
    color:var(--brand-ivory); font-size:clamp(16px,1.85vw,20px); max-width:32ch; margin:0 auto; text-shadow:0 1px 16px rgba(0,0,0,.3); letter-spacing:.01em; }
   /* must outrank .imagine-photo img{display:block} */


  /* hairline: ivory, with the faintest dark edge so it survives both images */

  /* handle: 44px hit box, 26px visible ring, no disc, no shadow */

  /* labels: lower corners, out of the caption's way */

  /* caption sits clear of both labels */  /* above the hairline: no strikethrough at mid positions */

  /* keyboard control: focusable, never captures pointer or touch */

  @media (max-width:720px){
  }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){
  }

  /* ---- Could This Work For You — reflective questions, same
     fragment-line treatment used across the site for short phrases,
     given here as questions rather than statements. ---- */

  /* ---- Understanding the Opportunity — practical detail, still
     presented as prose rather than a spec sheet. Sub-headings stay
     small and quiet so the page never tips into "brochure." ---- */
  .practical-group{ margin-top:12px; }
  .practical-item{ padding:19px 0; border-top:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.06); }
  .practical-item:first-child{ border-top:none; padding-top:0; }
  .practical-item h3{ font-size:clamp(18px,1.9vw,21px); margin-bottom:11px; }
  .practical-item p{ color:var(--soft); font-size:16px; line-height:1.8; max-width:56ch; }

  /* ---- Things To Consider — balanced points, same quiet list
     treatment, no warning icons or red text. ---- */
  .considerations{ margin-top:10px; }
  .considerations p{ color:var(--soft); font-size:16px; line-height:1.85; max-width:58ch; margin-bottom:16px; }
  .considerations p:last-child{ margin-bottom:0; }

  /* ---- Trusted Partners — premium placeholder. Reads as a promise,
     not an empty state; no logos, no "coming soon" badge. ---- */
  .partners{ position:relative; background:var(--cream); }
  .partners::before{ content:''; position:absolute; top:0; left:0; right:0; height:10vh;
    background:linear-gradient(180deg, var(--paper) 0%, rgba(248,245,236,0) 100%); pointer-events:none; }
  .partners::after{ content:''; position:absolute; bottom:0; left:0; right:0; height:10vh;
    background:linear-gradient(0deg, var(--paper) 0%, rgba(248,245,236,0) 100%); pointer-events:none; }
  .partners .article{ position:relative; z-index:1; padding-top:12vh; padding-bottom:12vh; text-align:center; }
  .partners .kicker{ font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.16em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--soft); opacity:.8; margin-bottom:24px; }
  .partners h2{ max-width:none; margin:0 auto 20px; font-size:clamp(22px,2.6vw,30px); line-height:1.35; }
  .partners p{ margin:0 auto; max-width:52ch; }
  .partners .partner-frame{ margin:48px auto 0; max-width:420px; padding:38px 32px; border:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.10); border-radius:2px; }
  .partners .partner-frame p{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-style:italic; color:var(--accent); font-size:16px; line-height:1.75; max-width:none; }

  /* ---- FAQ — elegant native accordion. No JS required for the
     interaction itself, keeping this section resilient and fast; the
     .reveal fade-in still applies on scroll like everything else. ---- */
  .faq-list{ margin-top:8px; }
  .faq-item{ border-top:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.06); }
  .faq-item:last-child{ border-bottom:1px solid rgba(31,59,46,.06); }
  .faq-item summary{ list-style:none; cursor:pointer; padding:21px 0; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:24px; }
  .faq-item summary::-webkit-details-marker{ display:none; }
  .faq-item summary h3{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-weight:500; font-size:clamp(17px,1.8vw,19px); font-style:normal; transition:color .3s ease; }
  .faq-item summary:hover h3{ color:var(--accent); }
  .faq-item .icon{ flex-shrink:0; width:20px; height:20px; position:relative; }
  .faq-item .icon::before, .faq-item .icon::after{ content:''; position:absolute; background:var(--accent); opacity:.75; border-radius:2px; transition:transform .35s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1), opacity .35s ease; }
  .faq-item .icon::before{ left:0; top:9px; width:20px; height:1.5px; }
  .faq-item .icon::after{ left:9px; top:0; width:1.5px; height:20px; }
  .faq-item summary:hover .icon::before, .faq-item summary:hover .icon::after{ opacity:1; }
  .faq-item[open] .icon::after{ transform:rotate(90deg); opacity:0; }
  .faq-item .faq-a{ padding:0 0 24px; color:var(--soft); font-size:16px; line-height:1.8; max-width:58ch; }

  /* ---- quiet tier — used on FAQ (and shares its language with Partners
     and Related): muted kicker, smaller heading, so these sections recede
     rather than compete with the emotional/editorial moments above them. ---- */
  .quiet-section .kicker{ color:var(--soft); opacity:.8; }
  .quiet-section h2{ font-size:clamp(22px,2.6vw,30px); line-height:1.35; max-width:22ch; }

  /* ---- Related Discoveries — three cards; kept quiet (photo + tiny
     kicker + title) so it invites exploration rather than selling. ---- */
  .related{ background:var(--paper); padding:10vh 7vw; }
  .related-head{ max-width:1040px; margin:0 auto 48px; text-align:center; }
  .related-head .kicker{ font-size:12px; letter-spacing:.16em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--soft); opacity:.8; margin-bottom:20px; }
  .related-head h2{ font-size:clamp(23px,2.8vw,32px); }
  .related-grid{ max-width:1040px; margin:0 auto; display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr); gap:34px; }
  /* TWO-CARD RAIL — local modifier, this document only. Applied where the
     duplicate Garden Discovery card was removed, so two cards centre in the
     rail instead of leaving a third column empty. Card width is preserved:
     324px at three-up, 333px here. */
  .related-grid.is-pair{ grid-template-columns:repeat(2, 1fr); max-width:700px; }
  .related-card{ text-decoration:none; color:inherit; display:block; }
  .related-card .thumb{ position:relative; width:100%; aspect-ratio:4/5.1; overflow:hidden; border-radius:2px; background:var(--ink);
    box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(31,59,46,.06); transition:box-shadow .5s ease; }
  .related-card .thumb img{ width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:cover; display:block; transition:transform 1s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); }
  .related-card:hover .thumb{ box-shadow:0 22px 44px -18px rgba(31,59,46,.28); }
  .related-card:hover .thumb img{ transform:scale(1.05); }
  .related-card .r-kicker{ margin-top:22px; font-size:11px; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--brand-sage); }
  .related-card h3{ margin-top:9px; font-size:clamp(17px,1.7vw,19px); transition:color .3s ease; }
  .related-card:hover h3{ color:var(--accent); }
  @media(max-width:820px){
    .related-grid{ grid-template-columns:1fr; gap:26px; max-width:420px; }
    .related-grid.is-pair{ grid-template-columns:1fr; max-width:420px; }
    .related-card .thumb{ aspect-ratio:3/2; }
    .related-head{ margin-bottom:40px; }
  }

  /* ---- closing statement (identical component to Homepage / About) ---- */
  .closing-line{ padding:21vh 7vw 19vh; text-align:center; background:var(--paper); }
  .closing-line p{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-style:italic; font-weight:400; font-size:clamp(19px,2.15vw,25px); color:var(--soft); max-width:36ch; margin:0 auto; line-height:1.7; letter-spacing:-.003em; }
  .closing-line .continue{ margin-top:22px; font-size:13px; font-style:normal; letter-spacing:.03em; }
  .closing-line .continue a{ color:var(--accent); text-decoration:none; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(79,107,74,.35); padding-bottom:1px; transition:border-color .35s ease; }
  .closing-line .continue a:hover{ border-color:var(--accent); }

  /* ---- footer (identical to Homepage / About) ---- */
  footer{ background:linear-gradient(180deg, var(--paper) 0%, var(--ink) 110px, var(--ink) 100%); color:#B7AF9C; padding:72px 7vw 40px; }
  footer b{ color:var(--brand-ivory); font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-weight:500; }
  .footer-inner{ max-width:1040px; margin:0 auto; }
  .footer-top{ display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:center; text-align:center; margin-bottom:64px; }
  .footer-mark{ display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:14px; margin-bottom:0; }
  .footer-mark img{ display:block; width:40px; height:40px; }
  .footer-word{ font-family:'Fraunces',serif; font-weight:600; font-size:21px; color:var(--brand-ivory); }
  .footer-cols{ display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(4, minmax(0,1fr)); gap:40px 32px; text-align:left; }
  .footer-col h2{ font-family:'Work Sans',sans-serif; font-size:11px; font-weight:500; letter-spacing:.14em; text-transform:uppercase; color:var(--brand-sage); opacity:.85; margin-bottom:20px; }
  .footer-col ul{ list-style:none; margin:0; padding:0; }
  .footer-col li{ margin-bottom:13px; }
  .footer-col li:last-child{ margin-bottom:0; }
  .footer-col a{ position:relative; color:#B7AF9C; text-decoration:none; font-size:14px; letter-spacing:.005em; transition:color .3s ease; }
  .footer-col a::after{ content:''; position:absolute; left:0; bottom:-3px; width:0; height:1px; background:currentColor; transition:width .35s cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1); }
  .footer-col a:hover{ color:var(--brand-ivory); }
  .footer-col a:hover::after{ width:100%; }
  .footer-col p{ font-size:14px; color:#B7AF9C; line-height:1.7; }
  @media(max-width:820px){
    .footer-cols{ grid-template-columns:repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)); text-align:center; gap:40px 24px; }
  }
  @media(max-width:520px){
    .footer-cols{ grid-template-columns:1fr; gap:36px; }
  }
  .footer-base{ margin-top:64px; text-align:center; font-size:11.5px; letter-spacing:.04em; color:#7C7565; }

  @media(max-width:720px){
    .d-hero-copy{ padding:0 8vw 8vh; }

   Each selector mirrors the specificity of the declaration it has to beat and
   wins on source order alone, so no !important is needed and no brand token
   moves. `.step-num` is genuinely unscoped; the other three are not, and the
   flat one-class form left all three measurably unchanged. The `.n` override
   is deliberately scoped to `.pb-step` only: `.atlas-figs .n` and
   `.platform-beats .n` on the homepage are var(--ink), already pass, and must
   not be touched. */
.step-num{ color:#557550; }
.related-card .related-kicker,
.related-card .r-kicker,
.pb-step .n{ color:#557550; }

/* E · reduced motion. This reuses the treatment the homepage already carries,
   whose author noted the 1.1s scroll-reveal "is a 1.1s fade and lift on every
   section ... Content is shown outright instead." The same principle is
   applied to the surfaces that never received it. Content must never depend
   on an animation finishing. */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){
  .reveal{ opacity:1 !important; transform:none !important; transition:none !important; }
  .article-section, .imagine-photo, .pb-preview, .related, .closing-line,
  .spark, .seam, .brand-mark, .brand-info{
    transition-duration:.01ms !important; animation-duration:.01ms !important;
    transform:none !important; opacity:1 !important;
  }
  /* The related-card thumbnail zooms on hover over 1s -- movement, so it is
     stilled. The sibling `.thumb` box-shadow transition is deliberately left
     alone: a shadow fade is not motion, and removing it would take away a
     hover affordance for no accessibility gain. */
  .related-card .thumb img{
    transition-duration:.01ms !important; transform:none !important;
  }
  html{ scroll-behavior:auto !important; }
}
/* PLOTNUA A11Y VISUAL v1 · END */

A PlotNua DiscoveryThe Borrowed Garden
A PlotNua Discovery

The Borrowed Garden

A corner of your garden could be exactly what somebody nearby is looking for.

Somebody a few streets away may be looking for ground to grow on.

The hardest thing to find, if you want to grow food, is somewhere to do it.
faqa: Where growers already are. Community gardens, local growing groups and council allotment lists are where people looking for ground are already looking. An early Irish attempt at the same problem. Homegrown.ie is a free Irish service that registers growers and garden owners separately and introduces them only when both sides agree, with exact addresses kept private. It is early and unproven: on its own published figures, which carry no review date, it had 78 grower requests, three offers of space and no completed matches, and it is still recruiting its first ten hosts. The insurance cover it hopes to arrange is not in place. Worth knowing about, not yet a working route, and PlotNua has no relationship with it. Write it down anyway. Nothing obliges you to, but the six things you agreed, on one page, signed by both of you, costs nothing, prevents most disagreements, and puts on record that this is permission to use ground rather than a letting.

The distinction that matters. A letting gives the other party the right to exclude you from the ground. Permission to use a part of a garden you still walk through is a different thing, and Irish courts look at how an arrangement works in practice rather than at the words on the page. So the protection is not a form of words — it is continuing to use your own garden. In practice. Keep the route through, keep the rest of the garden in normal use, and agree visiting hours rather than handing over a key to the whole property. None of this is a guarantee of any particular legal classification, and nothing here is legal advice. Your insurer. Liability to visitors is standard on an Irish household policy, but Allianz states plainly that visitors to your home for business purposes are not covered on a standard home policy, and money changing hands is exactly the sort of detail an insurer will want to know about. Ask before anyone starts, not after.

Growing is not development. Growing vegetables in a garden is not development, so no planning question arises. Anything built — a shed, a polytunnel — is treated exactly as if you had put it there yourself, and the usual rules apply. Beds lift. Raised beds sit on top of the ground and can be taken away. Ask for beds rather than dug ground if you want the lawn back, and agree at the start who restores the area. Ending it. A growing season is the natural unit. Agree the notice either of you gives and what happens to anything still in the ground, and the end of the arrangement is a conversation rather than a dispute.

blocks: What if the quiet corner was the part somebody needed?
Most gardens have a corner that is barely used. Somebody nearby may have been looking for exactly that.
You do not have to give up the garden. You choose the part you are comfortable sharing, you decide whether to start at all, and it stays yours to end.
For somebody without a garden, it could be somewhere to grow.
They may live only a few streets away. Neither of you currently knows the other exists.

Fingal County Council manages approximately 900 allotments across four sites, and did not accept new applications for Powerstown or Turvey for the 2026 season because those waiting lists were full. Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown is not accepting new applications for either of its sites — 136 plots at Goatstown, 95 at Shankill — under a council notice dated September 2024.

Which part You decide what part of the garden you are comfortable sharing. Together you agree the practical boundaries, access and how the space will work. A useful growing space is smaller than people expect, and it is worth saying early if you would rather nothing permanent went up.
Coming and going Agreed hours, and an agreed way in. Side access matters more than anything here. If the only route is through the kitchen, choose a different corner.
How long A growing season is the natural unit. Agree the notice either of you gives, and what happens to anything still growing.
Produce and costs A share of the harvest is the commonest arrangement. Agree who provides compost and timber, and whether there is an outside tap.
Cut every fortnight. Used twice a year.
Three things worth settling first.
Access Keep using the garden, and it stays your garden. What matters is how the arrangement actually works rather than what it is called. Walking through your own ground is the protection.

Insurance Tell your insurer before anyone starts. Cover for visitors is standard on an Irish household policy, but somebody growing food in your garden is not an ordinary social visit. One phone call settles it.
Money Payment is optional, and it is income. Plenty of arrangements involve no money at all. If you do take a seasonal payment, it is income and is taxable in the normal way.

The grower. Ground now rather than a place on a list.
You. A garden that is looked after, more interesting to stand in, and producing something. The vegetables can be the smaller half of it.

What if PlotNua could help you find each other?
Starting with an Eircode, a future version of PlotNua could identify whether a property has potentially shareable growing space, and show that people nearby are looking for somewhere to grow.
You would decide whether to explore it. If both sides were interested, PlotNua could help make a safe introduction.

Take part
Two ways to take part
Two short checks, one for each side. No address, and nothing to measure.
I have garden space to share
Four short questions about the part you could share, how somebody would reach it, and how you’d use it yourself. At the end, you can choose to join the Garden Owner Register.
I’m looking for somewhere to grow
Four short questions about where you are, how far you’d go, how much space and when. At the end, you can choose to join the Grower Register.
Which part could work, how somebody reaches it, and what you keep.
Whether anyone within walking distance is looking. PlotNua has not verified a live Irish route for this, and does not pretend to have one.
Only if both sides want one. Nothing would be shared before that.
Neither check sends your details anywhere. Both registers are expressions of interest only: free, private and non-binding. Nothing is matched or arranged.
Recommendations cannot be bought, and payment never determines who appears or ranks more highly.
